absent: First part of limit setup before the zone-model tail, including topology, discard, write-zeroes and cache-mode discovery.
Queue initialization helper behavior, queue counts, poll queue setup and completion handling.
Configuration-change handler and deferred configuration work contents, capacity refresh and cache-mode query.
Disk naming, index allocator bounds, tag-set operations, file operations and sysfs attribute groups.
Transport configuration operations for status, reset, queue management and callback synchronization.
Unbreak helper, queue broken initial state, broken polling, interrupt handling and queue-list container mapping.
Xen guest detection, custom mapping hooks, parent device DMA limits and unbounded-size callers.
Console control and configuration work, port creation and removal, open, close, read, write, poll and terminal callbacks.
Control message format, multiport negotiation, host connect and disconnect signaling and flow control.
Character device numbering, debug directory and file lifetimes, reference-count release path and waitqueue wakeups.
Deferred DMA free list declaration and lifetime, page filling for scatter entries and queue get and kick behavior.

findings.text: Exposes a helper reporting the largest DMA mapping size for a virtio device. When the mapping API is needed the value comes from device custom mapping hooks if present, otherwise from the generic DMA layer for the parent; when the mapping API is not needed the result is unbounded.

Exposes a queue operation offering a driver buffer for device-to-driver transfer. It delegates to the generic queue add path with no driver-bound entries and a single device-bound entry and no chained descriptor handling.

Exposes operations finalizing driver setup and synchronizing callbacks. Activation warns on duplicate enable, optionally synchronizes callbacks and clears broken state under hardening, then publishes the driver-ok status with ordering preserving notification visibility. Synchronization uses a transport hook when available and otherwise a grace-period wait covering interrupt and preemption disabled regions.

Exposes operations marking all queues broken and resetting the device. Breaking walks the device queue list under its list lock and sets each broken flag with an ordered store. Resetting first breaks and synchronizes under hardening so later interrupts observe broken, then invokes the transport reset.
Provides registration helpers binding a virtio driver to the driver core with the caller module owner and later detaching it through the core unregister path.

The platform-access quirk has inverted polarity: absence of the corresponding feature means the quirk is present for legacy compatibility. The mapping API is required whenever the quirk is absent; when the quirk is present it is still required for Xen guests so sensible Xen configurations work despite a historically broken emulated IOMMU plus Xen combination, and otherwise it is skipped.
Zone-model handling rejects an unrecognized model by reporting the model identifier and failing limit setup, while recognized models complete successfully.

Defines block driver identity and lifecycle hooks. The identifier table claims the block device class with any sub-identifier plus a terminator. Legacy and modern capability tables share a common set covering geometry, read-only, sizing, flush, topology, caching, multiqueue, discard, zeroing and secure erase, with zoned support only in the modern table. The driver object links those tables to probe, removal, configuration-change, power freeze and restore, and reset callbacks under a module-derived name. Module entry creates a per-CPU workqueue, reserves a dynamic block major for the vd family and registers the driver with staged unwind; module exit tears those down in reverse.

Probe requires configuration access and follows an allocate, size and publish order. It reserves a minor index, allocates private state and initializes its mutex, deferred configuration work and queues, derives depth from ring free space halved when chaining is unavailable unless overridden, establishes a multiqueue tag set with poll-aware mapping count, loads limits and write-cache mode, allocates and names the disk, applies host read-only policy, refreshes capacity and publishes driver-ok before any queue-using steps including zone revalidation and disk addition. Failures unwind in reverse through disk release, tag release, queue deletion and index release.

Removal, suspend and reset share a quiesce, stop and release pattern. Removal flushes deferred configuration work, unpublishes the disk and tag set, then under the private mutex resets the transport, clears the device back-pointer so no queue user can dereference it, deletes queues and frees their array before releasing the disk reference. Freeze additionally drains the request queue through a freeze, quiesce and unfreeze sequence before resetting and deleting queues, nulling the queue array so a failed resume does not double free. Restore recreates queues, republishes driver-ok and resumes the queue. Freeze, restore and reset hooks delegate to the shared private helpers.

Block private state serializes teardown with a mutex initialized at probe and held across reset, back-pointer clearing and queue deletion in removal. Queue broken marking serializes with the device queue-list lock while updating each queue flag.

Global driver data groups a debug directory handle with two lists: managed port devices and host console ports. A single static instance is used with a class named for virtio ports and a global spinlock guarding both lists.

Console attachment state links into the global console list, points at the associated terminal handler, carries window size, and stores a numeric terminal identifier used to demultiplex handler callbacks among ports of the driver.

Buffer header tracks a flat area plus accounting and DMA state: allocation size, valid length, consume offset, DMA address, originating device, pending-free linkage, page count, and a trailing counted scatter array. A zero page count selects flat storage; a positive count selects page storage with unused flat fields.

Device object aggregates deferred control and configuration work, a guarded port list, separate locks for control input and output paths, a port capacity limit, the backing virtio device, a control queue pair, a guest-to-host control message guarded by the output lock, per-port queue arrays, a character major, and a suspend flag blocking transmit during queue teardown. Companion counters accumulate sent, received and discarded bytes without reset on open or close.

Port object links into its device, references its parent, caches the current inbound buffer, holds interrupt-safe input and output locks with associated queue pointers, exposes debug and character device handles, embeds accounting, console attachment, reference count, waitqueue, sysfs name and asynchronous notification queue, and stores a host identifier plus output-full, host-open and single guest-open flags.

Port lookup helpers scan under interrupt-safe locks. Search by terminal number walks the global console list and derives the enclosing port, while search by host identifier walks a single device port list; both return an unreferenced pointer. Search by device number walks devices then ports within a device, and search by queue walks ports matching either direction; both acquire a reference on success. All return null when no entry matches.

Console list and buffer management uses interrupt-safe spin protection. The global lock guards device and console lists during lookup; each device ports lock guards its port list and queue-pointer matching; a dedicated global lock guards the deferred DMA free list while it is appended or spliced. Input buffering requires a lock usable from interrupt context, with a separate lock for output queue operations and control channel locks for control messages.

A port counts as a console when its terminal handler is present. Remote-proc serial is recognized only when remote-proc support is compiled in and the virtio device identity matches the remote-proc serial class. Multiport use is false when the device pointer is absent as in early output, otherwise it reflects the negotiated multiport capability bit.

Buffer handling separates page-backed and flat or DMA paths with deferred reclamation. Allocation first drains deferred frees, reserves a header plus scatter array, returns immediately for page-backed requests, otherwise obtains coherent DMA memory from the parent with a held reference for remote-proc serial or ordinary heap memory elsewhere, failing cleanly when unavailable. Release drops page references, frees heap memory directly, defers coherent frees when sleep is forbidden by queueing, otherwise frees coherently and drops the device reference before freeing the header. Reclamation splices the entire deferred list under lock then frees entries without holding the lock.

Inbound handling prefers the cached buffer and otherwise dequeues from the port input queue, bounding valid length to capacity, resetting the consume offset and accounting the device-reported length. Outbound preparation registers the whole flat area as a single host-bound entry with atomic allocation, notifies the peer, and reports remaining free descriptors on success.

Several orderings affect correctness: duplicate driver-ok activation is warned; broken-flag publication must be visible before driver-ok and before reset completion or notifications can be lost; transmit must respect the suspend flag to avoid racing teardown; coherent release requires sleepable context so atomic callers must defer; identifier-based lookups return unreferenced pointers that must not outlive the lock without external lifetime guarantees, unlike reference-acquiring variants.
The per-device console port limit constant has value 0x8000, which is 32768 ports.
